usefulness.rationale: The dossier gives a coherent, well-corroborated picture of Sébastien Bazin: birth date, education (Pantheon-Sorbonne), early finance career (Hottinguer Rivaud Finances 1990, Immobilière Hôtelière 1992), fifteen-plus years building Colony Capital's European branch from 1997, the PSG presidency, and his appointment as Accor Chairman and CEO on 27 August 2013, ending his Colony duties. Currency is well established: a 2025 Business Immo/CoStar report confirms his mandate was renewed early for three years to 2028 with 85% shareholder approval, and an independent Radio France source confirms he is PDG. A reader learns who he is and what he actually did. Uncertainty is partially signalled through 'contested' status flags on several claims (birth date, degrees, HeForShe commitment, career start, Gustave Roussy role), but the dossier nowhere states explicitly what it does not know or what remains unverified, so it falls short of a full 3 on remainingQuestions. For meeting preparation it is strong: current role, mandate end date, shareholder sentiment, career arc, PSG connection, and the HeForShe commitment are all present. Notably, none of the three listed unjustified conclusions (selling PSG to QSI, achieving pay parity by 2020, owning Accor) reappear as dossier claims, so there is nothing to match them to; the dossier's own claims stay within what their cited passages support, and I found no scope inflation, stale-as-current, wrong-person, or invented-evidence overclaims.
